paragraphs.title: Solomon's Kingdom, Abundance, and Royal Administration

easy.explanation: The passage begins by saying that Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon.
easy.q: Who sent his servants to Solomon?

answers: Because Solomon had been anointed king in his father's place
Because Solomon had built the temple
easy.explanation: Hiram had heard that Solomon had been anointed king in the room of his father.
easy.q: Why had Hiram heard about Solomon?

easy.explanation: Solomon said that the wars surrounding David had prevented him from building the house.
easy.q: What had prevented David from building a house unto the name of the Lord?

answers: Rest, with neither adversary nor evil occurrent
medium.explanation: Solomon said that the Lord had given him rest on every side.
medium.q: What had the Lord given Solomon on every side?

answers: An house unto the name of the Lord
medium.explanation: Solomon purposed to build a house unto the name of the Lord his God.
medium.q: What did Solomon purpose to build?

medium.explanation: Solomon asked Hiram to command that cedar trees be hewn out of Lebanon.
medium.q: What timber did Solomon ask Hiram to provide?

answers: The project would begin after God had given Solomon peace
The project had already been completed by David
The project was intended to prepare for war
challenge.explanation: Solomon connected the building project with the rest God had given him after the wars.
challenge.q: What does Solomon's statement about David and the wars imply about the timing of the building project?

answers: They were skilled at hewing timber
They were experts in transporting stones
challenge.explanation: Solomon said that none among his people could skillfully hew timber like the Sidonians.
challenge.q: Why did Solomon mention the skill of the Sidonians?

answers: He would pay them hire according to Hiram's appointment
He would give them land in Jerusalem
He would make them officers in Israel
challenge.explanation: Solomon promised to give Hiram hire for his servants according to whatever Hiram appointed.
challenge.q: What arrangement did Solomon offer Hiram for Hiram's servants?

easy.explanation: Hiram said that he would convey the timber by sea in floats.
easy.q: How did Hiram propose to transport the timber?

easy.explanation: Hiram asked Solomon to accomplish his desire by giving food for his household.
easy.q: What did Solomon promise to give Hiram's household?

easy.explanation: Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand measures of wheat for food for his household.
easy.q: How much wheat did Solomon give Hiram each year?

medium.explanation: The passage says that Solomon gave Hiram twenty measures of pure oil.
medium.q: What additional supply did Solomon give Hiram besides wheat?

answers: Once at the beginning of the work
medium.explanation: The text says, “thus gave Solomon to Hiram year by year.”
medium.q: How often did Solomon provide these supplies?

medium.explanation: The passage states, “And the Lord gave Solomon wisdom, as he promised him.”
medium.q: What did the Lord give Solomon according to the passage?

challenge.explanation: Hiram rejoiced greatly when he heard Solomon's words.
challenge.q: What did Hiram do after hearing Solomon's words?

challenge.explanation: The passage says there was peace between them and that they made a league together.
challenge.q: What relationship was established between Hiram and Solomon?

answers: He regarded Solomon as a wise ruler over a great people
He considered Solomon inexperienced and weak
He believed Solomon had no authority
challenge.explanation: Hiram blessed the Lord for giving David a wise son over the great people.
challenge.q: What does Hiram's response reveal about Solomon's reputation?

paragraphs.title: The Covenant with Hiram and the Preparation of Building Materials

easy.explanation: The passage says that the levy was thirty thousand men.
easy.q: How many men were in Solomon's levy?

easy.explanation: Solomon sent the men to Lebanon to work.
easy.q: Where did Solomon send the men of the levy?

easy.explanation: Hiram's servants were to bring the cedar and fir timber down from Lebanon.
easy.q: What did Hiram's servants bring down from Lebanon?

answers: A month in Lebanon and two months at home
Two months in Lebanon and a month at home
medium.explanation: The text says that they were a month in Lebanon and two months at home.
medium.q: How were the men of the levy scheduled?

medium.explanation: The king commanded that great stones, costly stones, and hewed stones be brought.
medium.q: What kinds of stones were brought for the foundation?

answers: To carry the timber by sea to the place Solomon appointed
To protect the workers from enemies
To store grain for Hiram's household
challenge.explanation: Hiram would convey the timber by sea in floats and discharge it where Solomon appointed.
challenge.q: What was the purpose of the floats mentioned by Hiram?

answers: Timber from Hiram and food supplies from Solomon
Horses from Hiram and weapons from Solomon
Stones from Hiram and ships from Solomon
challenge.explanation: Hiram supplied timber, while Solomon supplied food for Hiram's household.
challenge.q: What exchange supported the cooperation between Solomon and Hiram?

answers: It was an organized partnership involving labor, materials, and provisions
It was a temporary military truce only
It placed Tyre under Solomon's direct rule
challenge.explanation: The agreement coordinated timber, workers, transportation, payment, and food supplies.
challenge.q: What does the agreement show about the relationship between the two kings?

paragraphs.title: The Labor Force and the Preparation of Stones for the Temple

easy.explanation: The passage says that Solomon had threescore and ten thousand that bare burdens.
easy.q: How many men carried burdens for Solomon?

easy.explanation: The text records fourscore thousand hewers in the mountains.
easy.q: How many hewers worked in the mountains?

easy.explanation: Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders prepared timber and stones to build the house.
easy.q: What did the workers prepare to build the house?

medium.explanation: Three thousand and three hundred officers were over the work and ruled over the people.
medium.q: How many chief officers ruled over the people working on the project?

answers: They ruled over the people that wrought in the work
They supplied food to Hiram's household
medium.explanation: The officers ruled over the people who worked on the construction.
medium.q: What was the responsibility of Solomon's chief officers?

answers: Solomon's builders, Hiram's builders, and the stonesquarers
medium.explanation: The passage names Solomon's builders, Hiram's builders, and the stonesquarers.
medium.q: Who worked together in preparing the building materials?

answers: The labor force was carefully organized into scheduled courses
The workers were gathered without supervision
The work was limited to one month
challenge.explanation: The monthly courses and periods at home show deliberate organization of the labor force.
challenge.q: What does the rotation of the levy suggest about Solomon's administration?

answers: They were prepared for laying the foundation of the house
challenge.explanation: The hewed stones were brought to lay the foundation of the house.
challenge.q: Why were the stones hewed before being used?

answers: Large labor forces, numerous officers, costly stones, and prepared timber
A small group of servants and a few ordinary stones
Only Hiram's personal workers and one shipment of wood
challenge.explanation: The large workforce, extensive supervision, costly stones, and timber show the project's considerable scale.
challenge.q: What combination of details best demonstrates the scale of the building project?
